column1: # Kemp, Chick, Campbell and Hendrie (2008), Figs 8 and 9, the 'Bb Schmid' curve (with bell): DIGITIZED FROM RASTER FIGURES, NOT A MEASURED TABLE.
# Source: J. Kemp, J. Chick, M. Campbell and D. Hendrie, 'Acoustic pulse reflectometry for the measurement of horn crooks', Proceedings of Acoustics'08 Paris,
#   pp. 962-964, http://www.conforg.fr/acoustics2008/cdrom/data/articles/002669.pdf. Figs 8 and 9 show the bore profile (internal diameter against axial distance from the
#   mouthpiece receiver) of a modern Bb/Eb-alto double horn with rotary valves and a screw-on bell by Engelbert Schmid (Germany): curves 'Bb Schmid' (with bell), 'Bb Schmid no bell'
#   and 'Eb Schmid no bell', the main valves not depressed. This table is the first curve.
# Stated by the source [M]: bell connection exactly 70 mm; the with-bell and no-bell Bb curves diverge at a diameter of about 60 mm (plane-wave algorithm, so the bell end is not claimed
#   accurate); error bound for gradual-flare tubes about +-0.1 mm at 1 m and +-0.8 mm beyond 2 m; main tuning slide 11.9 mm (12.5 mm where partly pulled out; the reconstruction shows 12.2 mm);
#   first change valve at 580 mm, second at 720 mm, the Bb extra tubing ends at 1495 mm; discontinuities near 1200 mm (tuning slide and water keys).
# Method [R]: pdfimages -j of pages 4 and 5 gives two 560 x 420 px JPEGs (Fig 9: im-006, Fig 8: im-005). Axes calibrated by least squares on the plot-box ticks found as dark pixels inside
#   the bottom and left edges: Fig 9 x 4.6083 mm/px (9 ticks, residual rms 0.263 px = 1.21 mm, max 0.444 px), y 0.02632 mm/px (7 ticks, residual 0.000 px: the ticks sit on whole pixels);
#   Fig 8 x 8.4033 mm/px (7 ticks, rms 0.247 px = 2.08 mm, max 0.286 px), y 0.27198 mm/px (9 ticks, rms 0.285 px = 0.078 mm, max 0.434 px). Curve pixels by colour mask (blue minus max(red, green)

#   above 55, the JPEGs being dark); legend rectangles masked out; skeleton = weighted centroid per pixel column where the curve spans at most 4 rows and per pixel row where it spans at most 4 columns;

#   stations by linear interpolation: x = 20 to 1860 mm every 20 mm from Fig 9, 1880 to 2600 mm every 20 mm and 2610 to 2770 mm every 10 mm from Fig 8. The scripts of the run (digitise_schmid.py and axes_probe.py of the lane's scratch
#   directory) are NOT committed: the method written here is the whole account of it in the repository.
# Columns: x_mm; diameter_mm (internal, with-bell curve); figure; source_curve ('pooled green/red' where the blue curve is drawn under the others); threshold_range_mm = the range of the station

#   value when the colour-mask threshold is scaled by 0.7 and 1.4; d_green_no_bell_mm and d_red_eb_mm where those curves share the path (their difference from the blue is the reflectometer's own repeatability
#   on x = 200 to 1400 mm: median 0.106 mm, max 0.795 mm); reading_error_1px_mm = sqrt((1 px vertical)^2 + (local slope x 1 px horizontal)^2); source_bound_mm where the source states one; flags.
# Uncertainty: reading error 0.03 to 0.07 mm for x < 1880 mm, 0.3 to 0.7 mm for 1880 to 2520 mm, 1 to 4.3 mm for 2560 to 2770 mm; and above about 60 mm diameter (x about 2660 mm) the source's own

#   plane-wave reflectometry is unreliable. The narrowest spikes (20 mm spacing) are aliased and are not smoothed. x = 0 to 20 mm is the receiver end and has no station here; the card starts its profile
#   from the red curve's first pixel, 7.66 mm at x = 6 mm.
